declarations.checkedType: agent(body: unknown, context: string, method: string, token: string of private, url: string) -> unknown with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Issue an authenticated Google API call — @method@ to @url@ carrying @body@ under the `Bearer` @token@ —
and return the reply parsed as JSON. @body@ is the request document as a value tree, sent as
application/json, or `null` for a call that carries none (a GET, a DELETE); a 2xx with an empty body (a
204 No Content) answers `null`, and a 2xx body that is not JSON throws `json.parse_error`. A non-2xx
throws `http.api_failure` classified by `http.classify_status` — a 401 or 403 is `http.auth_error`, every
other status `http.api_error` — carrying the failing status, @context@ and Google's own body as
`message`. Google also spends 403 on quota exhaustion, and that 403 is still read as auth: a replayed
quota 403 costs one wasted retry, where reading a revoked token as a quota problem costs the recovery.
declarations.name: call

parameters.documentation: The absolute API URL, query string included.
parameters.label: url

parameters.documentation: The request document as a value tree, or `null` for a call that carries none.
parameters.label: body

parameters.documentation: Which call this is, in the caller's words — it rides on a failure beside the status.
parameters.label: context

parameters.documentation: The resolved Google access token, asked for by the calling package's own `credential`.
parameters.label: token

body.description: The request document as a value tree, or `null` for a call that carries none.

context.description: Which call this is, in the caller's words — it rides on a failure beside the status.

token.description: The resolved Google access token, asked for by the calling package's own `credential`.

url.description: The absolute API URL, query string included.

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse`.

declarations.checkedType: agent(accumulated?: array[unknown], base_url: string, context: string, item_key: string, page_token?: string, token: string of private) -> array[unknown] with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Drain a paginated Google listing: GET @base_url@, take the items it carries under @item_key@, follow
`nextPageToken` to exhaustion, and answer every page's items concatenated in page order. @base_url@ must
already carry its query string, since `&pageToken=` is appended to it; a page carrying no @item_key@ array
contributes nothing, so an empty listing is the empty list. The items come back unparsed, as `unknown`,
and @token@ is resolved once by the caller and reused across the drain's pages.
declarations.name: paged

parameters.documentation: The listing's first-page URL, query string included — `&pageToken=` is appended to it.
parameters.label: base_url

parameters.documentation: The key of the page's item array: "messages" for a `messages.list`, "items" for an `events.list`.
parameters.label: item_key

parameters.documentation: Which listing this is, in the caller's words — it rides on a failure beside the status.
parameters.label: context

parameters.documentation: The resolved Google access token, asked for by the calling package's own `credential`.
parameters.label: token

parameters.documentation: The drain's own state: the page to fetch, `null` for the first. Not for a caller to pass.
parameters.label: page_token

parameters.documentation: The drain's own state: the items the pages already read contributed. Not for a caller to pass.
parameters.label: accumulated
